market_summary: Tech stocks tumbled on November 12 as Nvidia's board met to potentially oust CEO Jensen Huang following reports of extramarital affairs, raising major uncertainty at the world's dominant AI chipmaker. Nvidia shares fell 8% in extended trading and over 7% in European markets, erasing roughly $600 billion in market value since the investigation was announced. Elsewhere, Alphabet's Google Cloud surged 103% to $30.7 billion in Q3 revenue with operating margins expanding dramatically to 36.2%, driving consolidated revenue up 25% with 13 consecutive quarters of double-digit growth. Singapore's banking sector showed mixed Q3 results: OCBC beat estimates with 3% profit growth, while DBS and UOB missed forecasts as net interest margins compressed. Singapore Exchange reported October derivatives at six-month highs with securities turnover up 32% year-on-year, while Singapore Airlines continues absorbing losses on its Air India investment.

items.headline: Nvidia board met to decide whether to oust CEO Jensen Huang over alleged affairs
items.summary: <cite index="5-1">Nvidia's board met on Wednesday to decide whether to oust CEO Jensen Huang following reports of two extramarital affairs involving its dominant AI chipmaker</cite>. <cite index="5-4,5-5">Nvidia's stock slid around 7% in early Frankfurt trading on Thursday, with the company having lost about $600 billion in market value since the board announced its investigation</cite>.

items.headline: Alphabet's Google Cloud revenues doubled to $30.7 billion in Q3 2026 with operating margins expanding to 36.2%
items.summary: <cite index="19-4">Google Cloud delivered record growth as revenues increased 103% to $30.7 billion, led by strong growth in Google Cloud Platform across enterprise AI infrastructure and enterprise AI solutions</cite>. <cite index="23-1">Google Cloud operating income more than tripled year over year with operating margin increasing from 23.7% to 36.2%</cite>.

items.headline: OCBC beats Q3 2026 expectations with 3% profit growth as only Singapore bank to meet estimates
items.summary: <cite index="38-1">OCBC was the only one to meet expectations in 3Q26, with net profit rising 3% year-on-year to S$2.04 billion</cite>. <cite index="38-2">DBS reported a 5% year-on-year decline in 3Q26 net profit, while UOB's 3Q26 profit also came in below expectations</cite>.

items.headline: DBS Q3 2026 net profit declined 5% year-on-year, missing analyst expectations
items.summary: <cite index="40-2">DBS Q3 2026 net profit dipped 2% to S$2.95 billion</cite> with broader results showing DBS among banks facing net interest margin pressure and earnings headwinds in the quarter.

items.headline: UOB Q3 2026 profit missed expectations as earnings pressured by margin compression
items.summary: <cite index="41-13">UOB reported S$1.25 billion profit for Q3 2026, missing expectations</cite>, marking the second major Singapore bank to underperform forecasts in a weak quarter for the sector.

items.headline: Singapore Airlines' Air India investment carrying value falls to S$799.9 million from S$1.135 billion in six months
items.summary: <cite index="12-1,12-2,12-3">As of March 31, 2026, Singapore Airlines' Air India investment carrying value was SGD 1.135 billion, declining to SGD 799.9 million by September 30, 2026, representing a reduction of approximately SGD 334.7 million in just six months</cite>.

items.headline: SGX October securities turnover rose 32% year-on-year to S$44.8 billion with derivatives reaching six-month highs
items.summary: <cite index="30-1">Securities turnover rose 32% year on year and 6% month on month to S$44.8 billion, while derivatives daily average volume increased 17% month on month and 8% year on year to 1.6 million contracts, its highest level since April</cite>.

items.headline: US technology stocks fall sharply as Nvidia's CEO crisis triggers broad tech selloff
items.summary: Nvidia's uncertainty over CEO Jensen Huang's future pressured the broader technology sector on November 12. Major US tech indices declined alongside Asian markets as investors reassessed risk in AI-dependent mega-cap stocks amid broader macro uncertainty.
